note: A measurement record, not a capture set. This entry was corrected by measuring a claim it already made; no new frame was needed, because the figure it wanted already exists and is recorded in techniques-colour-clash.json. Governed by 198x/decisions/capturing-published-software.md.

measurements.tested_claim: Strategy 2, 'Block alignment': "Force all moving sprites to occupy whole 8x8 cells. The sprite snaps to the grid ... Atic Atac and Sabre Wulf both use cell-aligned movement and avoid clash by snapping."
measurements.verdict: FALSE for Sabre Wulf. The player sprite moves three pixels per frame and stands on positions that are almost never cell boundaries.
measurements.controls: The game's menu offers 1/2 PLAYER, 3 KEYBOARD, 4 KEMPSTON, 5 CURSOR JOYSTICK, 6 INTERFACE II, 0 START. There is no define-keys step, so KEYBOARD uses a fixed mapping the menu never states. CURSOR JOYSTICK was chosen instead precisely because its mapping IS known and fixed: 5 left, 6 down, 7 up, 8 right. Each direction was confirmed individually before measuring rather than swept, after a key sweep caused a false 'hang' finding on emu198x#872.
measurements.method: Load the tape, select 1 PLAYER then CURSOR JOYSTICK then START, settle, then hold 5 (left) and screenshot EVERY frame for 60 frames. The player is the only pure-white object inside the arena, so his left edge is the minimum x of white pixels within the playfield.
measurements.result: Left edge per frame: 120, 120, 120, 120, 120, 119, 117, 115, 112, 109, 107, 103, 100, 97, 94, 91, 88, 85, 82, 79, 76, 73, 70, 67, 64, 61, 58, then held at 58 against an obstacle. Per-frame deltas are -1, -2, -3 and -4; the sustained rate is three pixels per frame. Of the 24 distinct positions occupied, only 120, 88, 64 and 112 fall on an 8-pixel boundary — the rest are mid-cell.
measurements.what_it_means: Sabre Wulf does not avoid clash by snapping to the grid. It avoids clash the way techniques-colour-clash.json already records with a published frame: the playfield is black and every colour is pushed out into an impassable border, so a sprite moving at three pixels per frame never shares a cell with anything coloured. The mechanism named in the entry and the mechanism the game uses are different mechanisms.
measurements.not_tested: Atic Atac was named in the same sentence; see the next measurement, which was run after this one on Steve's prompting.

measurements.tested_claim: The same sentence in Strategy 2: "Atic Atac and Sabre Wulf both use cell-aligned movement and avoid clash by snapping."
measurements.verdict: FALSE on both halves. The Knight moves one to two pixels per frame and stands off the cell grid, and he visibly clashes with the room's scenery — so the game neither snaps nor avoids clash. With Sabre Wulf also removed, Strategy 2 has no example left in this entry.
measurements.controls: Menu: 1 KEYBOARD, 2 KEMPSTON JOYSTICK, 3 CURSOR JOYSTICK, 4 KNIGHT, 5 WIZARD, 6 SERF, 0 START GAME. Same shape as Sabre Wulf and the same reasoning: CURSOR JOYSTICK for a mapping that is fixed and known (5 left, 6 down, 7 up, 8 right) rather than a KEYBOARD mode whose mapping the game never states. Played as the Knight.
measurements.method: Hold 5 (left) and screenshot every frame for 60 frames. The Knight is the only pure-white object inside the room, so his left edge is the minimum x of white pixels within the play area, excluding the right-hand HUD panel which also carries white.
measurements.result_movement: Left edge per frame: 56 held, then 55, 53, 53, 49, 47, 45, 43, 43, 39, 37, 37, 33, 24, 24, 24, 24, 20, then held at 20. Per-frame deltas of -1, -2 and -4. Ten of the thirteen distinct positions are off the 8-pixel grid.
measurements.result_clash: capture/verify-clash.py --sprite, baseline s022 (Knight clear of the scenery): frame s040 reports one object across 7 cells, six drawn in (255,255,255) and one in (255,0,255) at cell (3,10); frame s042 reports 8 cells, seven white and one magenta at (2,10). The minority ink matches the standing art in the very cells carrying it, which is the same signature the Dizzy capture produced for the colour-clash entry. The Knight is being drawn in the scenery's ink.
measurements.what_it_means: Atic Atac is cited in the wild as a clash-avoiding game and it is not one. It moves smoothly and it clashes. It has been removed from Strategy 2 rather than reassigned, because 'embraces the clash' is a claim about intent and nothing measured here speaks to intent.
measurements.note_on_s038: A sweep across neighbouring frames also flagged two larger multi-ink objects (red/magenta, green/red). Those are NOT reported as clash: they are more likely the room's own multi-coloured art moving relative to the baseline, and they were not investigated. Only the two frames above, where the minority ink is a single cell of scenery the Knight has entered, are claimed.

figure: The entry now shows sabre-wulf-black-arena.png, which already existed and is recorded in full — dump, SHA-1, timeline — in techniques-colour-clash.json. One frame, one provenance record, two entries making different claims about it. Recapturing the same frame into a second directory would have duplicated the artefact and split its provenance.
